display.title: Episode 426: The Flickering Flame (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Sefirah show without music: respect for one another, why counting days teaches the value of time, Shema with a young guest, and a shoemaker's lamp that teaches a great tzaddik about teshuvah.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi explains why this show begins without music: during Sefirah we remember the students of Rabbi Akiva who died because they did not show each other respect. He lists ways to practice respect for parents, teachers and friends, to look for the good in others and pursue peace, and says that unity and good example are our answer to 'Ad mosai'. Next he teaches that counting the Omer shows how precious each day is, with the story of a girl named Miriam who keeps crying over a lost dime: we cannot get back lost time, only use well the time we have. A boy of almost five leads the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time tells of a great tzaddik, Rabbi Yisroel, stranded in a snowstorm, who finds an old shoemaker still at work by a lamp he overfilled with oil. The shoemaker's words, 'as long as the light still burns, one can still repair', become a lesson about teshuvah. The show ends with the Tzivos Hashem Lag BaOmer parade and carnival, choosing a Torah-true summer camp, and Shabbos candle times.
display.lesson: Time is Hashem's precious gift: use every day better than the day before, and as long as the light burns, we can still repair and do teshuvah.

date.note: Estimate was 29 Nissan. Lag BaOmer 'Sunday, May 13' still ahead; candles 7:44, Shabbos ends 8:54 fit Friday 11 May 1990. One week after episode 425.

advisories.note: Rabbi Akiva's students die in a plague as a punishment for not respecting one another.

segments.title: Why No Music: Rabbi Akiva's Students and Respect

segments.title: Counting Days: The Precious Gift of Time
